title: SDKs enterprise prioritization and triage — bridging language gaps, auth patterns, and streaming ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Collect, triage, and prioritize incoming enterprise requests for SDKs and client libraries focusing on: (1) language support gaps (lang bindings and platform idioms), (2) enterprise auth patterns (token rotation, SSO/OAuth, mTLS, KMS integration), and (3) streaming ergonomics (reconnect, backpressure, partial/resumable responses). Goal is a repeatable rubric and a small initial delivery that reduces top customer friction while minimizing engineering lift.

Problem statement: Over the last 12 months we have 42 distinct requests from enterprise customers asking for SDK libraries, language runtime support, or enhancements to streaming behavior and auth integrations. Signal is concentrated in three themes: stronger first‑party bindings for Go and .NET, SDK-managed enterprise auth workflows (token refresh + rotation + audit hooks), and streaming ergonomics for resumable sessions and better client-side buffering. These gaps increase support load, slow time-to-value for enterprise POCs, and create security/ops inconsistencies across deployments.

Scope: This ticket defines intake criteria, prioritization rubric, and a candidate MVP implementation plan:
- Intake: standardized intake form, minimum reproducible example, customer impact score, and security checklist.
- Rubric: combine customer-reported impact, revenue/ARR signal, engineering cost estimate, and compliance risk into a single prioritization score.
- MVP: deliver official Go and C# minimal SDKs implementing: typed client, streaming helper with reconnect/backpressure primitives, and a pluggable auth adapter supporting API key rotation and OAuth client-credentials flows.

Acceptance criteria:
- Documented intake form published to internal Confluence and support playbook.
- Prioritization rubric computed and applied to the backlog (top 5 SDK requests scored).
- Prototype Go and C# SDKs with streaming helper and auth adapter: unit tests, sample apps, and one enterprise pilot customer onboarded (Acme AI or FinServCorp).
- Telemetry contract for SDKs (token usage, error classes, reconnect events) defined and agreed with Observability team.

Trade-offs considered:
- Language breadth vs. depth: supporting 6 languages increases market coverage but triples maintenance surface. We prioritize Go and C# first due to highest enterprise signal and lower runtime surface area compared with Python and Node where community libs exist.
- Auth centralization vs. SDK-managed: central auth service reduces duplication but increases infra burden. Choose hybrid: SDKs expose a pluggable adapter interface and ship a default "managed refresh" adapter that handles API key rotation and OAuth refresh tokens; enterprises can override with a central token provider integration.
- Streaming complexity: full gRPC streaming surface is large. MVP will provide an ergonomic HTTP/WS-based streaming helper that supports resumable checkpoints and backpressure, with an extension point for future gRPC/wasm-based implementations.

Next steps / plan:
1) Publish intake form + add to support triage (owner: Product Operations).
2) Run scoring on existing backlog and mark top-5 (owner: PM).
3) Engineering spike to evaluate streaming helper APIs and authentication adapter pattern (owner: ENG runtime). 2-week spike.
4) Deliver Go + C# SDK prototypes and internal sample apps; onboard 1 pilot customer.

Success metrics: SDK adoption for enterprise signups (+20% POC conversion), reduction in support tickets related to auth/streaming (-30% over 3 months), pilot SLA compliance and telemetry signals within expected thresholds.

Notes: This ticket is intentionally scoped to create a replicable pattern that can be used to onboard additional languages (Rust, Swift) without redoing the auth or streaming primitives.
